brief.summary_1line: Rama, distressed by public criticism of Sita despite her proven innocence, tells Lakshmana he must take her away to a forest hermitage.

image_candidates.scene_text: Rama sits with a grief-stricken face before his brothers, declaring that public censure forces him to send the innocent Sita away.
Rama recalls Sita stepping into the blazing sacrificial fire while the gods and sages watch as witnesses to her purity.

deep.rich_summary: Rama, seated among his sorrowful companions, confesses the anguish troubling his heart: public gossip about Sita’s purity. Although he recounts how Sita proved her innocence after Ravana’s abduction—entering the sacred fire and being vindicated by Agni, the gods, and celestial witnesses—Rama fears the corrosive power of public dishonor. As a king of the Ikshvaku line, he believes a ruler must remain beyond reproach, even at terrible personal cost. Tormented by the criticism of the people, he concludes that reputation and royal duty outweigh his private certainty of Sita’s innocence. The speech builds toward a tragic decision: he will separate from Sita despite loving her and knowing she is pure. The passage reveals the painful tension between dharma as kingly duty and personal loyalty.

highlight_spans.why: The chapter opening sets the somber tone, showing Rama addressing his court in visible grief.
Rama recalls Ravana’s abduction of Sita and his own victory, anchoring the moral crisis in earlier epic events.
The pivotal recollection of Sita entering the fire and being vindicated by divine witnesses.
Rama declares he fears dishonor so deeply he would renounce even his life and loved ones—revealing the emotional and ethical stakes.
The tragic turning point where Rama concludes he must separate himself from Sita despite her innocence.

top_scenes.scene_text: Sita standing within blazing sacred fire while Agni rises and the gods, winds, sun, and moon bear witness to her innocence.
Rama in a dim royal hall, face stricken with grief as he addresses Lakshmana and the gathered court about the rumors against Sita.
